question: ‘Vrittayata’ is a major sub-division of ________ style of temple architecture.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dravidian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Vrittayata' refers to the circular plan of temple architecture which is a significant characteristic of the Dravidian style.
 
• The Dravidian style of temple architecture is predominantly found in Southern India.
 
• It is characterized by pyramid-shaped towers (Vimanas) and large temple complexes.
 
• Some of the famous Dravidian temples include the Brihadeshwara Temple in Thanjavur and the Meenakshi Temple in Madurai.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara Style**

 
 
• This style is prevalent in Northern India.
 
• It features beehive-shaped towers called Shikharas.
 
• Examples include the temples of Khajuraho and the Sun Temple at Konark.
 
 
 
• **Hoysala Style**
 
 
• This style is found in the Karnataka region.
 
• It is known for its star-shaped platforms and intricate carvings.
 
• Famous examples include the Chennakesava Temple at Belur and the Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu.
 
 
 
• **Vijayanagara Style**
 
 
• This style developed under the Vijayanagara Empire in South India.
 
• It combines elements of both Dravidian and Nagara styles.
 
• The Virupaksha Temple at Hampi is a notable example.
